dish: Monthly-changing Japanese course of the chef's own creation
w: Promoted to Two MICHELIN Stars (2026): a Japanese course that changes every month, entirely the chef's own creation.
One MICHELIN Star Chinese restaurant in Okazaki cooking with a seasonal Kyoto aesthetic.
One MICHELIN Star offshoot of Ogata where its apprentices cook — known for hot-pots and dishes grilled over a shichirin brazier.

dish: Flower-garnished hassun platters drawn from festival foods
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand Japanese restaurant run by a former fishmonger; seasonal menus whose hassun platters, garnished with flowers, recall traditional festival foods.

dish: Tempura dressed with chopped onion and mustard (Tenjaku style)
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand tempura-kaiseki house inherited from the chef's grandfather in Nishijin; its signature dresses tempura in chopped onion and mustard.

dish: Straw-smoked fish; whole-cut grilled venison and duck
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand char-grill izakaya run by a former French chef — straw-smoked fish and venison and duck grilled as whole cuts.
Michelin Bib Gourmand sushi shop in Nakagyō delivering Kyoto-style sushi at a modest price.
Michelin Bib Gourmand Japanese kitchen whose inventive, patient cooking includes a salad dressed with heshiko mackerel.

dish: Thick saba-zushi roll; duck-scented minced cutlet
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand washoku with ingenious touches — fluffy potato salad, a minced cutlet with a hint of duck, and a thick saba-zushi roll.
Michelin Bib Gourmand French regional bistro in Tanaka — fish soup, goat's-cheese salad, sautéed frog.
One MICHELIN Star (2026) soba house in Saga by Seiryō-ji (Saga Shakadō), Arashiyama.
Michelin Bib Gourmand yōshoku house keeping the previous generation's classics — gratin and cutlets — with French specials on the blackboard.

dish: Kinshi-don — eel under ribbons of omelette
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand eel house founded at the end of the Edo period as a river-fish wholesaler; the fourth-generation chef's kinshi-don, under thin-cut omelette ribbons, is renowned.

dish: Shigure-meshi with sea-bream sashimi in sesame sauce
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand casual offshoot of the three-star Kikunoi; its house speciality is shigure-meshi rice topped with sea bream sashimi in sesame sauce.

dish: Shrimp wontons; stir-fried squid and asparagus
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand Cantonese kitchen — shrimp wontons, stir-fried squid with asparagus, seasonal soups.

address: 140 Dōyū-chō, Sakaimachi-dōri Sanjō-sagaru, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto 604-8118, Japan
w: Kyoto's classic kissaten, in business since 1940; the retro main shop serves a 'Kyoto breakfast' available only at the flagship.

dish: Nishin soba — kake soba topped with sweet-simmered dried herring
address: Beside Minami-za, Shijō-dōri, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan
w: Founded in 1861 as a theatre teahouse; in 1882 the second-generation owner invented nishin soba and moved beside the Minami-za kabuki theatre — the dish has been a Kyoto speciality ever since.

dish: Soba in a dashi of Kyoto well water
w: Founded in 1465 and billed as Japan's oldest soba restaurant; stock made with Kyoto well water and freshly boiled buckwheat noodles.
